recognize_zh: 骨髓切片中央有一團淡粉紅、細胞核呈卵圓或腎形的類上皮組織球（epithelioid histiocytes）聚集，周圍混有淋巴球與嗜酸性球（箭頭），為骨髓肉芽腫。
features: Aggregate of epithelioid histiocytes with abundant pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and indistinct cell borders
Histiocyte nuclei oval to reniform with vesicular chromatin and small nucleoli
Admixed eosinophils with bright red granules (arrows) and small lymphocytes
No necrosis or multinucleated giant cells in this field
Surrounding hematopoietic marrow and fat spaces
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy shows a loosely formed aggregate of epithelioid histiocytes with abundant pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and oval to reniform vesicular nuclei. Admixed eosinophils (arrows) and small lymphocytes are present at the periphery. No caseous necrosis or multinucleated giant cells are seen in this field. Findings are consistent with a bone marrow granuloma; special stains for organisms (AFB, GMS) and clinical correlation are recommended to determine etiology.

ddx.vs: Lipogranulomas are small, centered on fat vacuoles with foamy macrophages, and are incidental, unlike this compact epithelioid aggregate.
Hodgkin involvement shows Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells (CD30+, CD15+) within a fibrotic mixed infiltrate, which are not seen here.
Mast cell aggregates are spindled with clear cytoplasm, often paratrabecular with eosinophils, and are CD117/tryptase positive rather than CD68-positive histiocytes.
LCH cells have grooved, coffee-bean nuclei and are CD1a/langerin positive, typically with numerous eosinophils.
